title: campaign-recon.json — qe campaign recon + plan artifact (format v2)
description: Machine-readable campaign plan: the contract between a qe campaign's scan stage (recon) and its execute stage (ADR 0006 'qe campaign homes into the four planes'). Formalizes the three lenses of the proven hand-built shape (studio-campaign-recon.json, 2026-08 studio E2E campaign): a capability inventory with file:line citations, a reference to the generated environment manifest (the fail-closed preflight input), and a dependency-ordered scenario ladder whose rungs carry pass criteria (terminal state + artifact + consumer state) and per-rung claim ceilings. Scenario BODIES live as scenario-format markdown files (skills/qe/refs/scenario-format.md) — this artifact orders and binds them; it never replaces that format. The sibling evidence contract (scenario_evidence + claim_level) is owned by wicked-ledger (manifest 2.1, docs/SCHEMA-CONTRACT.md there), deliberately a different owner. Format v2 (TH-16 + TH-22, ONE shared bump): rungs gain the optional 'isolation' annotation (shares-state | exclusive | stateless) consumed by the crew-side scenario→CampaignNode mapping (TH-9), and 'desktop' rungs become stub-eligible because scenario-format v1.1 adds the desktop category (tiered T0–T3). spec:1 plans remain valid — every v2 addition is optional, and 'isolation' requires spec 2 (extra-invariant check in scripts/qe/campaign_plan.py).

spec.description: Campaign-recon format version. 1 = original (no rung isolation; desktop rungs were not stub-eligible). 2 = the TH-16 + TH-22 shared bump: adds the optional per-rung 'isolation' annotation and desktop stub-eligibility (scenario-format v1.1). Backward compat: v1 plans still validate; a rung carrying 'isolation' requires spec 2 — enforced as an extra-invariant check (scripts/qe/campaign_plan.py), like ladder order. Bumps move through garden's release train (same discipline as wicked-pack.schema.json's spec field).

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the recon artifact was produced.

repo.description: Target repository — a local path or owner/name.

ref.description: Git ref or sha the recon was performed against. Selector/route claims are only as fresh as this ref — executors must verify against the BUILT artifact actually served, never source recon alone.

surface_url.description: Base URL of the live app probed during recon, if any (e.g. 'http://127.0.0.1:7701/').

sources.description: Where the inventory came from. Honest-degradation marker: recon on a repo without an estate graph MUST say estate:'unindexed' and rely on docs+probe only — never silently substitute.

estate.description: 'indexed' = capability inventory seeded from estate's code graph (route/handler/component nodes, injected edges). 'unindexed' = graph unavailable; inventory is docs+probe-derived and coverage claims must say so.

docs_recall.description: True when mem/search docs recall contributed entries.

live_probe.description: True when live-app probing (health endpoints, DOM landmarks) contributed entries.

capabilities.description: Capability inventory (surface-inventory lens): one entry per user-facing capability of the target.

environment_manifest.description: Reference to the campaign's environment manifest (binary resolution paths, ports, isolated state dirs, forbidden fabrication flags, artifact identity, platform_support). The manifest is its own generated artifact enforced by the fail-closed preflight stage — this is a reference, never an inline copy.

ref.description: Path (relative to this artifact) or identifier of the environment manifest.

sha256.description: Optional lowercase hex SHA-256 of the referenced manifest, pinning the exact preflight contract this plan was generated against.

scenarios.description: Dependency-ordered scenario ladder (test-plan lens). Producers MUST emit topological order: every id named in a rung's deps appears EARLIER in this array, and never references an unknown id. JSON Schema cannot express that invariant — validators enforce it as an extra-invariant check (see tests/qe/test_campaign_recon_schema.py).

citation.description: file:line citation backing a recon claim, e.g. 'client.ts:304' or 'HealthRailSection.tsx:21-27,100'.

id.description: Stable kebab-case capability id. Rungs bind to it via capability_ids; ledger scenario ids derive from capability-id + slug so flake history accrues across re-runs.

surface.description: What the user sees/touches — component, page, affordance (e.g. 'Projects CRUD — /projects (ProjectsPage), NewProjectModal').

apis.description: The endpoints/events behind the surface, with file:line citations inline (e.g. 'POST/GET /projects (client.ts:560-578)').

test_shape.description: What a PASS looks like — rendered state + wire evidence (e.g. 'PASS = new project card on /projects; wire = 200 {project}').

needs.description: Preconditions: daemons, ports, fixtures, prior capabilities.

citations.description: First-class file:line citations backing this entry (in addition to any inline in apis/test_shape).

source.description: Primary origin of this entry: estate code graph, docs recall, live probe, or human input.

status.description: Doc/site-derived claims enter as 'proposed' pending human confirmation; only code-graph- or probe-verified entries are 'verified'.

claim_ceiling.description: The strongest claim_level a PASS on this rung may assert, per wicked-ledger's manifest-2.1 claim_level enum (certified | machinery-verified | skipped). 'skipped' is an outcome-only level, never a plannable ceiling. A rung whose user journey is API-substituted caps at 'machinery-verified' — certify the user journey, not the proxy.

pass_criteria.description: The three proofs a PASS requires (launch ≠ done): a terminal state reached, an artifact produced, and a consumer observing that state. All three are mandatory for every rung.

terminal_state.description: The terminal state that must be reached and how it is proven (e.g. 'run status completed in the durable event log, not just a 200 on launch').

artifact.description: The artifact that must exist as evidence (e.g. 'evidence bundle JSON downloaded; row present in a later GET /projects').

consumer_state.description: The downstream consumer state that must reflect the change (e.g. 'dashboard route renders the project after a hard reload').

id.description: Scenario id, unique within the campaign (e.g. 'S11', 'projects-crud-ui').

category.description: Execution surface of the rung — the campaign-plan taxonomy. NOTE: this is not the scenario-format category enum (api|browser|perf|infra|security|a11y|cli|equivalence, plus desktop as of scenario-format v1.1); the rung's scenario file keeps its own format category. Generated stubs map api→api, ui→browser, desktop→desktop. Desktop rungs execute per the tier ladder in skills/qe/refs/scenario-format.md: T0 crew-governed PTY (proven now), T1 playwright _electron (when a target exists), T2 computer-use exploratory (ALWAYS reviewer-graded, macOS first), T3 deterministic native automation (deferred in writing).

capability_ids.description: Capability inventory ids this rung certifies.

deps.description: Ids of rungs that must PASS before this one runs. May be empty. Every entry MUST name a rung that appears earlier in scenarios[].

isolation.description: Shared-state isolation class of this rung — the machine-consumed annotation for TH-9's scenario→CampaignNode mapping when the campaign runs as a parallel DAG (wicked-core campaign.rs via crew POST/GET /api/v1/campaigns). Absent = 'shares-state', the conservative default: an unannotated rung is assumed to mutate state shared with other rungs in the same target instance (the proven campaign reality — projects, repos, and runs accumulate in one daemon) and must never run concurrently with another rung against that instance. 'stateless' = the rung touches no shared mutable state OR namespaces every fixture it creates (unique project/repo names via QE_FIXTURE_NS — the runner's fixture-namespacing default, scripts/qe/runner/README.md); safe to parallelize with other stateless rungs against the same instance. 'exclusive' = the rung needs sole access to the entire target environment (daemon kill/restart, migration, recovery rungs); the mapping MUST either add DAG serialization edges or give the node its own isolated profile (fresh WICKED_HOME / --db / --bus-db — the campaign runbook's proven recipe). Requires spec 2. Until a scheduler mapping actually consumes this annotation, campaigns MUST run with max_concurrency: 1 — correct, just slow; the constraint is explicit, never accidental.

scenario_path.description: Path to the persisted scenario-format markdown file (v1.0 or v1.1) this rung executes (relative to the campaign root). The plan binds scenarios; it never inlines them.

status.description: Doc-derived rungs enter as 'proposed' (pending human review, per the incident-to-scenario pending-review pattern); 'confirmed' rungs are executable.

notes.description: Free-text execution notes (disclosed substitutions, known drift, timing).
